rounds.t: Scleroderma, skin layers, and cell junctions

q.s: A 45-year-old woman has thick, tight skin on her arms, trunk and face that progressed over 1 year, with new shortness of breath. Which antibody is associated with her form of disease?
e: Correct. Diffuse scleroderma; also anti-RNA polymerase III.

q.s: A woman with CREST syndrome is most likely to have which antibody?
What does the "E" in CREST stand for?
e: Correct. Calcinosis, Raynaud, Esophageal dysmotility, Sclerodactyly, Telangiectasia.

q.s: A patient with diffuse scleroderma develops sudden severe hypertension and acute kidney injury. Which drug class is used?
The triad of systemic sclerosis is:
o: Autoimmunity, noninflammatory vasculopathy and collagen deposition with fibrosis

q.s: Which mnemonic lists the epidermal layers from surface to base?
o: "Come, let's get sunburned" — corneum, lucidum, granulosum, spinosum, basale

q.s: What are the three layers of the skin?
Tight junctions are composed of which proteins?
Loss of E-cadherin, a component of adherens junctions, promotes:
Adherens junctions connect which cytoskeletal elements of adjacent cells?
Autoantibodies against desmoglein 3 cause:
Which junctions use connexons to allow electrical and chemical communication between cells?
Autoantibodies against hemidesmosomes cause which disease?
Integrins maintain the basolateral membrane by binding which molecules?
o: Collagen, laminin and fibronectin in the basement membrane

q.s: Sebaceous glands secrete by which mechanism?
Mammary glands secrete by which mechanism?
o: Apocrine (part of the cell is pinched off)

q.s: Salivary and eccrine sweat glands secrete by:
Limited scleroderma differs from diffuse scleroderma by:
o: Rapid progression and early organ involvement
Skin involvement confined to fingers and face, with a more benign course
e: Wrong. Raynaud is part of CREST.

q.s: GI involvement in scleroderma causes:
o: Decreased peristalsis and LES tone causing dysphagia and heartburn

q.s: Which pulmonary complications occur in scleroderma?
A flat, well-circumscribed area of color change smaller than 1 cm is a:
Vitiligo lesions larger than 1 cm that are flat are called:
A raised solid lesion smaller than 1 cm, such as a neurofibroma, is a:
Psoriasis typically presents with raised lesions larger than 1 cm, called:
A fluid-filled blister larger than 1 cm, as in bullous pemphigoid, is a:
A transient smooth, raised lesion typical of hives is a:
Honey-colored dry exudate in impetigo is called:
Which lesion involves loss of epidermis without exposure of the basement membrane?
e: Correct. E.g., HSV, pemphigus vulgaris, SJS/TEN.
Wrong. Exposes basement membrane and deeper.

q.s: A decubitus lesion extending into the dermis and muscle is called:
Retention of nuclei in the stratum corneum is called:
Increased thickness of the stratum granulosum is characteristic of:
Epidermal accumulation of edematous fluid between cells is called:
Separation of epidermal cells is called:
Epidermal hyperplasia with increased stratum spinosum is called:
Abnormal premature keratinization, as seen in squamous cell carcinoma, is called:
Calluses show which microscopic change?
Chickenpox lesions that are small fluid-filled blisters smaller than 1 cm are:
Flaking of the stratum corneum, as in eczema and psoriasis, is called:
A vesicle filled with pus, as in pustular psoriasis, is a:
Which microscopic finding does psoriasis show?

rounds.t: Pigmented disorders and common skin conditions

q.s: A child has very pale skin, white hair and light eyes. Melanocyte numbers are normal. What is the defect?
o: Decreased tyrosinase activity or defective tyrosine transport
Failure of neural crest migration to the skin
e: Correct. Albinism; increased skin cancer risk.

q.s: A pregnant woman develops symmetric brown patches on her cheeks and forehead. Diagnosis?
e: Correct. "Mask of pregnancy"; also with OCPs.

q.s: A woman with type 1 diabetes and Hashimoto thyroiditis has patches of complete depigmentation around her mouth and hands. Mechanism?
A child has a white forelock, different-colored irises and congenital deafness. Diagnosis?
e: Correct. Defective neural crest differentiation into melanocytes.

q.s: An infant has greasy yellow scales on the scalp. Which organism may contribute?
Extensive seborrheic dermatitis in adults is associated with:
Which factor contributes to acne?
o: Cutibacterium acnes colonization of the pilosebaceous unit
e: Correct. Plus androgens and abnormal desquamation.

q.s: A 7-year-old with asthma has itchy, dry, lichenified patches in the antecubital and popliteal fossae. Diagnosis?
e: Correct. Flexural in children; face in infancy; ↑ IgE.

q.s: A woman develops an itchy rash under her belt buckle. What hypersensitivity type is this?
e: Correct. Allergic contact dermatitis to nickel.

q.s: Rough follicular papules on the backs of the arms caused by keratin plugging are called:
Junctional melanocytic nevi appear as:
A man with curly hair develops painful papules and pustules along his jawline after shaving. Diagnosis?
Scraping a silvery scale off a plaque on the elbow causes pinpoint bleeding. This is called:
Which histologic findings characterize psoriasis?
o: Acanthosis, parakeratosis, Munro microabscesses, increased spinosum and decreased granulosum
Increased stratum granulosum and sawtooth lymphocytes

q.s: Psoriasis is associated with:
A 40-year-old woman has facial flushing with alcohol and hot drinks, and red papules and pustules on her cheeks without blackheads. Diagnosis?
e: Correct. Complications include rhinophyma and eye involvement.

q.s: A 70-year-old has several brown, waxy, "stuck-on" lesions on his back. Biopsy shows proliferation of immature keratinocytes with keratin-filled cysts. Diagnosis?
A 65-year-old suddenly develops dozens of new seborrheic keratoses over a few months. What does this suggest?
o: Possible internal malignancy such as GI adenocarcinoma (Leser-Trélat sign)

q.s: Warts are caused by which pathogen?
Urticaria results from:
o: Mast cell degranulation with superficial dermal edema

q.s: A 70-year-old woman who had a mastectomy with chronic arm lymphedema develops purple nodules on the affected arm. Diagnosis?
Hepatic angiosarcoma is associated with exposure to:
A man with AIDS has red-purple skin papules. Biopsy shows a neutrophilic infiltrate and the organism is seen on silver stain. Diagnosis?
A 50-year-old man has a few small, bright red, dome-shaped papules on his trunk that have increased with age. Diagnosis?
A woman has an exquisitely painful, small red-blue lesion under her fingernail that hurts with cold. Diagnosis?
e: Correct. From modified smooth muscle of the glomus body.

q.s: A transplant recipient develops violaceous plaques on his legs and in his mouth. Which virus is associated?
How is Kaposi sarcoma distinguished from bacillary angiomatosis histologically?
o: Kaposi shows organisms on silver stain

q.s: A pregnant woman develops a rapidly growing, friable red nodule on her gum that bleeds easily. Diagnosis?
e: Correct. Associated with trauma and pregnancy.

q.s: An infant develops a red, raised lesion at 3 weeks of age that grows rapidly. What is its expected course?
o: Requires surgical excision in all cases

q.s: Kaposi sarcoma is classically seen in which groups?
o: Older Eastern European men, patients with AIDS and organ transplant recipients

q.s: Why is angiosarcoma often difficult to treat?
o: It is very aggressive and diagnosed late, making resection difficult

q.s: Angiosarcoma usually occurs in which locations?
o: Head, neck and breast areas in sun-exposed older adults

q.s: Which vascular lesion regresses spontaneously while the others do not?
Pyogenic granuloma is histologically a:
e: Wrong. Not infectious despite the name.

q.s: Which organism causes bacillary angiomatosis?
Kaposi sarcoma is a malignancy of which cell type?
Which organs besides skin are commonly affected by Kaposi sarcoma?
o: Mouth, GI tract and respiratory tract

q.s: Stewart-Treves syndrome refers to:
o: Cutaneous angiosarcoma developing after chronic lymphedema
Hepatic angiosarcoma after vinyl chloride exposure

q.s: Glomus tumors arise from cells involved in:
o: Thermoregulation (modified smooth muscle of the glomus body)

q.s: Bacillary angiomatosis is frequently mistaken for which tumor?
e: Correct. Distinguished by its neutrophilic infiltrate.

q.s: A 4-year-old has crusted, honey-colored lesions around his nose and mouth. His sibling has similar lesions. Which organisms are responsible?
Bullous impetigo is usually caused by:
A 60-year-old has a bright red, raised, sharply demarcated plaque on his cheek with fever. Which layer is infected?
Cellulitis is distinguished from erysipelas by:
o: Deeper dermal and subcutaneous involvement with less defined borders

q.s: A walled-off collection of pus within the skin is almost always caused by:
A diabetic man has severe leg pain out of proportion to a small area of redness, rapidly spreading violaceous bullae and crepitus. What is the appropriate management?
o: Emergency surgical debridement with broad-spectrum antibiotics

q.s: Crepitus in necrotizing fasciitis results from:
o: Methane and CO2 produced by bacteria

q.s: A newborn develops fever and widespread redness with sloughing of the superficial skin. Gentle rubbing separates the epidermis. Mucous membranes are spared. Diagnosis?
e: Wrong. Mucosa involved; split at dermal-epidermal junction.
Correct. Exotoxin splits the stratum granulosum.

q.s: Which layer is split by the exfoliative toxin in staphylococcal scalded skin syndrome?
A dental hygienist develops painful vesicles on her finger. Diagnosis?
A child has multiple small, pearly papules with a central dimple. Which virus causes them?
Molluscum contagiosum in adults may be:
A child has itchy lesions on the trunk in different stages, from vesicles to crusts, appearing in crops. Diagnosis?
Herpes zoster typically appears in what distribution?
A man with HIV has white, painless plaques on the lateral tongue that cannot be scraped off. Which virus is responsible?
How is oral thrush distinguished from hairy leukoplakia?
o: Thrush is painless and cannot be removed
Thrush occurs only on the lateral tongue

q.s: Necrotizing fasciitis is usually caused by:
o: Anaerobic bacteria, S. pyogenes or S. aureus (including MRSA)

q.s: Staphylococcal scalded skin syndrome is common in which groups?
o: Newborns and patients with renal insufficiency
e: Correct. The toxin is renally cleared.

q.s: Which infection is associated with fascia that is pale and friable with a "dishwater-gray" exudate?
Which virus causes both chickenpox and shingles?

rounds.t: Cutaneous mycoses and autoimmune blistering disorders

q.s: A child who plays with a new kitten has an expanding, scaly red ring on his arm with central clearing. KOH shows branching septate hyphae. Diagnosis?
Which organisms are dermatophytes?
A child has patchy hair loss with scaling and enlarged posterior cervical lymph nodes. Diagnosis?
Tinea cruris differs from tinea corporis because it:
o: Often lacks central clearing and occurs in the groin

q.s: Which type of tinea pedis is most common?
A young man has hypopigmented patches on his upper back that become more noticeable after a summer beach trip. KOH shows "spaghetti and meatballs." Why are the patches hypopigmented?
o: Malassezia lipid degradation produces acids that inhibit tyrosinase

q.s: What is the treatment for tinea versicolor?
o: Selenium sulfide and topical or oral antifungals

q.s: Onychomycosis is also called:
A 72-year-old has flaccid blisters that rupture easily, painful oral erosions and a positive Nikolsky sign. Which structure is targeted?
Biopsy of pemphigus vulgaris shows:
o: Intraepidermal acantholysis with a "row of tombstones"

q.s: Immunofluorescence in pemphigus vulgaris shows:
o: Linear deposits at the epidermal-dermal junction

q.s: An 80-year-old man has tense, itchy blisters on his thighs and trunk. His mouth is spared and the Nikolsky sign is negative. Immunofluorescence would show:
o: Linear IgG at the epidermal-dermal junction

q.s: Pemphigus vulgaris and bullous pemphigoid are both which hypersensitivity type?
e: Correct. IgG autoantibodies against tissue antigens.

q.s: Which blistering disease is more severe and potentially fatal?
Bullous pemphigoid blisters contain which inflammatory cells?
In pemphigus vulgaris, desmogleins connect keratinocytes in which layer?
Tinea versicolor is more common in:
Is Malassezia a dermatophyte?
o: No; it is a yeastlike fungus despite the name "tinea versicolor"

q.s: Dermatophyte infections are characteristically:
o: Pruritic, with septate hyphae on KOH preparation

q.s: Tinea corporis can be acquired from:
o: Contact with infected pets or farm animals

rounds.t: Other blistering disorders and cutaneous ulcers

q.s: A woman with chronic diarrhea and iron deficiency has intensely itchy grouped vesicles on her elbows, knees and buttocks. Biopsy shows IgA at the tips of dermal papillae. Which treatment is appropriate?
e: Correct. Dermatitis herpetiformis with celiac disease.

q.s: A 20-year-old has recurrent herpes labialis followed by "target" lesions with dusky centers on his palms and arms. Diagnosis?
e: Correct. Associated with HSV and Mycoplasma.

q.s: Erythema multiforme is associated with which infection?
Ten days after starting lamotrigine, a woman has fever, painful mucosal erosions of the lips, eyes and genitals, and skin sloughing over 20% of her body. Diagnosis?
In SJS and TEN, skin sloughing occurs at which level?
Toxic epidermal necrolysis involves more than what percentage of body surface area?
An infant develops blisters in the mouth during bottle feeding and blisters on the skin after minor friction. Which genes are most commonly mutated?
Which drugs are associated with erythema multiforme and SJS?
A 70-year-old with varicose veins has a shallow, irregular, weeping ulcer over the medial malleolus with surrounding brown discoloration. Diagnosis?
A smoker with claudication has a painful, punched-out ulcer on his toe. The foot is cold and hairless with absent pulses. Diagnosis?
A diabetic patient has a painless ulcer under the first metatarsal head with a thick callused rim. Diagnosis?
A bedbound patient develops an ulcer over the sacrum. Which complications are frequent?
Which ulcer type is associated with Charcot joints and claw toes?
Venous ulcers are associated with which skin change?
o: Stasis dermatitis with telangiectasias and edema

q.s: Pain level of arterial ulcers is typically:
Nikolsky sign is positive in which pair of conditions?
e: Correct. Also staphylococcal scalded skin syndrome.

q.s: Dermatitis herpetiformis is associated with which condition?
Target lesions in erythema multiforme show:
o: Concentric scaly rings with central clearing
Multiple rings with a dusky center showing epithelial disruption

q.s: SJS is usually caused by:
Venous ulcers are located in the:
o: Gaiter area, typically over the malleoli

q.s: An obese teenager with irregular periods has dark, velvety thickened skin on the back of her neck. With which condition is this associated?
e: Correct. Acanthosis nigricans; also PCOS, Cushing syndrome and visceral malignancy.

q.s: A 60-year-old thin man suddenly develops acanthosis nigricans and weight loss. Which malignancy should be considered?
A young woman with sarcoidosis has painful red nodules on her shins. What is the pathology?
Erythema nodosum is associated with all of the following EXCEPT:
e: Correct. Not listed; celiac is associated with dermatitis herpetiformis.

q.s: A child with atopic dermatitis has fine, fish-like scales on the extensor surfaces of the legs. Which gene is mutated?
A patient with hepatitis C has itchy, purple, flat-topped polygonal papules on his wrists, and lacy white lines on his buccal mucosa. Diagnosis?
Histology of lichen planus shows:
o: Sawtooth infiltrate of lymphocytes at the dermal-epidermal junction with hypergranulosis

q.s: A teenager has a single large scaly pink oval patch on his trunk, followed a week later by many smaller patches in a "Christmas tree" pattern. Management?
Which UV wavelength is dominant in sunburn?
Late radiation dermatitis, months to years after radiotherapy, shows:
o: Dermal fibrosis with homogenized collagen, vascular damage and telangiectasias

q.s: Using the rule of 9's, burns to the entire front and back of one arm and the entire front of the torso (chest and abdomen) cover about what percentage of body surface area?
In the rule of 9's, each entire leg accounts for:
A firefighter rescued from a burning building has singed nasal hairs and soot in his mouth. What complication should be anticipated?
o: Compartment syndrome of the arm only
Burn wound sepsis within an hour
Inhalation injury with airway edema and possible ARDS

q.s: A burn is red, blistered, painful to air and blanches with pressure. What depth is it?
A burn that is white, waxy, leathery and painless, with only deep pressure sensation, is:
A sunburn without blisters involves which layer?
A deep partial-thickness burn involves:
o: Epidermis and reticular dermis; does not blanch; perceives pressure only

q.s: Which of the 6 P's of lichen planus is correct?
o: Pruritic, purple, polygonal, planar papules and plaques

q.s: UVA is mainly responsible for:
Acute radiation dermatitis occurs within 90 days of radiotherapy and is caused by:
o: Apoptosis of basal keratinocytes and epidermal edema

q.s: A 70-year-old farmer has a pearly, pink nodule with rolled borders and telangiectasias on his nose. What is its typical behavior?
e: Correct. Basal cell carcinoma, the most common skin cancer.

q.s: Basal cell carcinoma is more common:
A kidney transplant recipient has an ulcerated red lesion on his lower lip. Biopsy shows keratin pearls. Diagnosis?
A man develops an ulcerated mass in a burn scar he has had for 30 years. Diagnosis?
o: Marjolin ulcer (SCC in a chronic wound)

q.s: Which exposure is occasionally associated with squamous cell carcinoma of the skin?
Small, rough, scaly red papules on the sun-exposed scalp of a balding man are premalignant lesions called:
e: Correct. Risk of SCC is proportional to dysplasia.

q.s: A 45-year-old has a mole that has changed in color and size, with irregular borders and a diameter of 9 mm. Which feature best predicts metastatic risk if this is melanoma?
Which tumor marker is used for melanoma?
Which melanoma subtype has the highest prevalence in people with darker skin tones?
e: Wrong. Most common overall in light skin.
Wrong. Sun-damaged skin of older adults.

q.s: Advanced melanoma with a BRAF V600E mutation can be treated with:
o: Vemurafenib (BRAF inhibitor) and immunotherapy such as ipilimumab

q.s: What is the primary treatment for melanoma?
Which ABCDE criterion refers to the size of a suspicious mole?
Which skin cancer is the second most common?

o: It is the most common skin cancer
It never spreads to lymph nodes
It is locally invasive, may spread to lymph nodes and rarely metastasizes

q.s: Which skin cancer is most often driven by an activating BRAF mutation?
Which feature is most typical of basal cell carcinoma?
o: Pearly nodule with telangiectasias and rolled borders
